artifacts.summary: All 7 plan phases implemented: corrected error-handling.md to name issue-record.sh, added a 16th seed class for infrastructure/transport unavailability, documented a general occurrence-collapse convention and a 10-citation render cap, added a push-based central-log library wired into both shared writers, implemented Sapience capture as a subclass with an honest MCP-tool-failure gap note, and closed Phase 7 COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS against two confirmed pre-existing, unrelated gate findings.

completion_data.completion_summary: Corrected the documented error-store contract to name issue-record.sh (the store actually written), added an infrastructure/transport-unavailable seed class, a general occurrence-collapse convention, a push-based central cross-repo log wired into issue-record.sh and events-append.sh with an owning-repo skip, a 10-citation render cap at the conclusion stage, and Sapience backend-failure capture implemented strictly as a subclass of that general mechanism. All four acceptance replays (Sapience 503 outage, central promotion, occurrence collapse, citation cap) passed against the real deployed scripts; measured promotion overhead ~17ms/call.

memory_candidates.content: When a fixture under test-X.sh copies a production script (e.g. issue-record.sh, events-append.sh) into a synthetic scratch tree, adding a new unconditional `source lib/<newlib>.sh` to that production script breaks EVERY existing fixture that doesn't also copy the new library -- under `set -euo pipefail`, a missing source target aborts the whole script before reaching any guarded call site. The fix is to guard the source call itself with a file-existence check and a no-op function-definition fallback, not to update every existing fixture. This was only caught by running the FULL test corpus (run-all.sh's gate 8), never by a narrower tier-justified suite subset -- a reminder that per-phase suite-subset verification cannot substitute for a full-corpus run before declaring a cross-cutting library change complete.

A test suite under scripts/tests/ that computes its own repo root via a hardcoded walk-up depth (e.g. `ROOT=$(cd "$CORE_DIR/../../../.." && pwd)`) silently breaks when invoked from a DIFFERENT depth than the one the walk assumed -- specifically, a depth tuned for the source-store path (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts, 4 segments from repo root) resolves to a path OUTSIDE the repository when the same suite runs from its deployed location (.claude/scripts, only 2 segments from repo root), which is exactly how run-all.sh's gate 8 invokes it. Symptom: downstream git/repo-relative computations return their own sentinel/fail-open value (e.g. gate_cache_implementation_digest returning CANNOT_COMPUTE) rather than an obvious error. Diagnostic recipe: echo the computed ROOT value under both invocation paths directly, and/or re-run the suite from its source-store copy -- if it passes there and fails only from the deployed copy, the walk-up depth is the suspect, not the suite's actual logic under test.

When a suite's SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST subject resolution is 'deploy-tree-first' (common_test_resolve_subject), a pending source-store edit that has not yet been redeployed will silently cause the suite to exercise the STALE deployed copy, producing a false read (pass or fail) unrelated to the actual edited logic. Before trusting such a result mid-task (before the eventual redeploy phase), temporarily overwrite the deployed copy with the edited source-store file(s), re-run the suite, then restore the deployed copy byte-for-byte (md5sum-confirmed) -- this gets a true read without prematurely redeploying or leaving the deployed tree in an inconsistent interim state. A suite whose resolution mode is 'source-store' instead (not deploy-tree-first) needs no such workaround since it always exercises the edited source directly.
